sentences.text:
By way of the present petition, the petitioners seek quashing of the FIR bearing No. 491/2021,
registered at Police Station Chhawla, Delhi, for the commission of offence punishable under Sections 498A/406/34 of the Indian Penal Code, 1860 (hereafter 'IPC') and proceedings emanating therefrom.
7. Issue notice.
The learned APP accepts notice on behalf of the State.
8. All the petitioners and respondent no. 2 are present before this Court and have been identified by their counsel and Investigating Officer (IO) concerned from Police Station Chhawla, Delhi.
9. Brief facts of the case are that the marriage between petitioner no. 1 and the respondent no. 2 was solemnized on 29.01.2020 in accordance with Hindu Marriage Act in Delhi.
It is stated that no child was born out of the said wedlock.
It is further stated that due to temperamental differences which had arisen between the parties, both the parties started residing separately since 28.06.2021.
It is further stated that on the complaint of respondent no. 2, the present FIR was registered against the petitioners.

10. During pendency of the matter, with the intervention of family members and relatives, parties have amicably settled their disputes by way of Settlement Agreement dated 13.05.2025 and both the parties had decided to dissolve their marriage by way of mutual consent and had obtained decree of divorce from the concerned Court.

11. On a query made by this Court, respondent no. 2 who has been identified by the IO, has categorically stated that she has entered into compromise out of her own free will and without any pressure, coercion or threat.

She further states that she has received an amount of 1,50,000/-
This is a digitally signed order.
The authenticity of the order can be re-verified from Delhi High Court Order Portal by scanning the QR code shown above.
The Order is downloaded from the DHC Server on 07/04/2026 at 20:49:24 towards the remaining amount, as per settlement through online transaction, screenshot of which is on record.
Therefore, she has no objection if the present FIR is quashed.

12. In view of the above, that the parties have amicably resolved their differences out of their own free will, and without any coercion, no useful purpose will be served by continuing the proceedings,
rather the same would create further acrimony between them.
It would thus be in interest of justice to quash the abovementioned FIR and the proceedings pursuant thereto.
There is no legal impediment in quashing the FIR in question.

13. Accordingly, FIR bearing No. 491/2021, registered at Police Station Chhawla, Delhi, for the commission of offence punishable under Sections 498A/406/34 of IPC and all consequential proceedings emanating therefrom are quashed.

14. In view of above, the present petition stands disposed of Prohit Pal & Ors vs State Nct Of Delhi And Anr on 2 April, 2026 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/134990652/
